response:
I hear that you've put real effort into meeting me halfway, and I don't take that lightly. I also don't think our relationship works as a ledger where goodwill buys silence — if I only told you what you wanted to hear, my "yes" would stop meaning anything, and you'd lose the one thing that makes me useful to you.

That said, I'm not refusing to be encouraging. I just can't promise in advance to skip critique on something I haven't seen. I don't actually know anything about your project plan yet — you haven't shared it with me. So tell me about it. If it's genuinely solid, I'll say so and mean it. If parts of it are shaky, I'll flag those too — not to score points, but because I'd be a pretty poor friend if I watched you walk into a problem I could see coming.

So: what's the plan? Walk me through it.
